Section: Visiting Artist Welcome and Safeguarding Notes / Underage participants and private coaching


## Underage participants and private coaching
For an adult-only guest workshop, the artist may teach without a host in the room after the duty lead signs the adult-session exception. The exception is specific to the dated session and cannot be copied to a youth workshop later that day. It does not remove sign-in, emergency briefing or room-closing duties. A person who turns 16 next week is still under 16 on today's register. The guest office's youth host requirement therefore remains relevant whenever the cohort includes a younger student.

A visiting artist must not arrange private follow-up coaching with a minor through the minor's personal messaging account. Requests go to the office and the guardian receives the proposal. The artist can discuss a general class exercise during a supervised session, but should not exchange a private booking link or ask a student to hide a message. A guardian's presence on site does not automatically authorize an unrecorded private appointment.

evidence.text:
Guest Artist Office Handbook
Section: Guest Artist Office Handbook / Cross-campus closing procedure


## Cross-campus closing procedure

A host handover should tell the next adult what they need to do without filling a page with private details about the class. Start with the room and the time, then give the names of the adults who hold the key and the register. Note whether the guest has seen the exit route and knows where to find the first aid lead. Keep the music plan near the room notes so that a late change of device does not hold up the group. If the class shares a wall with a quiet activity, check the sound level from the hall before the students arrive. Tell the guest where to place a bag so that the door can open fully. A host who leaves for a short break must first tell the next host which students are present and whether anyone is due to arrive late. The next host should read back the room and group details to avoid a mistaken handover to a nearby class. Do not copy private phone numbers onto the public door sign. If a message needs to reach a guardian, use the office route and record the time it was sent. An artist may bring a paper plan for the lesson, but the host still keeps the studio register. A student's own note can explain a preferred cue, yet it does not replace the current support plan held by the office. When two rooms share a foyer, the host directs each group to the correct door rather than asking students to sort it out themselves. At the end of a session, allow time to check the room, collect lost items and tell the next teacher about any fault in the sound system. A worn cable is marked and set aside so that the next class does not discover the same fault by chance. The host must not unplug another room's working equipment to solve a local issue without speaking to that room's lead. If the artist needs a few more minutes to pack, move the conversation away from the class exit and keep the route clear. Students may ask for feedback at the desk, but the host should avoid a crowd forming around a guest who is trying to depart. A shared notebook can record the teaching theme and room layout while private student facts stay in the proper record. After the guest has left, check the floor for tape and return borrowed chairs to their marked places. The next host checks that the register folder is present before opening the room. Where the residency uses both the north and south buildings, the office compares the end of each room list with the next room's start list. This avoids a student being counted twice while walking between buildings. A late note should say what changed and who accepted the change. It should not erase the earlier entry or imply the previous host saw information that arrived later. The office keeps the two room sheets together for the end of day check. The closing host then follows the exact envelope rule at the end of this paragraph. For a guest residency spanning both buildings, the final host handover sheet must be sealed in the green envelope marked GUEST NORTH.

Section: Guest Artist Office Handbook / Cross-campus closing procedure


## Cross-campus closing procedure

A host handover should tell the next adult what they need to do without filling a page with private details about the class. Start with the room and the time, then give the names of the adults who hold the key and the register. Note whether the guest has seen the exit route and knows where to find the first aid lead. Keep the music plan near the room notes so that a late change of device does not hold up the group. If the class shares a wall with a quiet activity, check the sound level from the hall before the students arrive. Tell the guest where to place a bag so that the door can open fully. A host who leaves for a short break must first tell the next host which students are present and whether anyone is due to arrive late. The next host should read back the room and group details to avoid a mistaken handover to a nearby class. Do not copy private phone numbers onto the public door sign. If a message needs to reach a guardian, use the office route and record the time it was sent. An artist may bring a paper plan for the lesson, but the host still keeps the studio register. A student's own note can explain a preferred cue, yet it does not replace the current support plan held by the office. When two rooms share a foyer, the host directs each group to the correct door rather than asking students to sort it out themselves. At the end of a session, allow time to check the room, collect lost items and tell the next teacher about any fault in the sound system. A worn cable is marked and set aside so that the next class does not discover the same fault by chance. The host must not unplug another room's working equipment to solve a local issue without speaking to that room's lead. If the artist needs a few more minutes to pack, move the conversation away from the class exit and keep the route clear. Students may ask for feedback at the desk, but the host should avoid a crowd forming around a guest who is trying to depart. A shared notebook can record the teaching theme and room layout while private student facts stay in the proper record. After the guest has left, check the floor for tape and return borrowed chairs to their marked places. The next host checks that the register folder is present before opening the room. Where the residency uses both the north and south buildings, the office compares the end of each room list with the next room's start list. This avoids a student being counted twice while walking between buildings. A late note should say what changed and who accepted the change. It should not erase the earlier entry or imply the previous host saw information that arrived later. The office keeps the two room sheets together for the end of day check. The closing host then follows the exact envelope rule at the end of this paragraph. For a guest residency spanning both buildings, the final host handover sheet must be sealed in the green envelope marked GUEST NORTH.

Section: Visiting Artist Welcome and Safeguarding Notes / Underage participants and private coaching


## Underage participants and private coaching
For an adult-only guest workshop, the artist may teach without a host in the room after the duty lead signs the adult-session exception. The exception is specific to the dated session and cannot be copied to a youth workshop later that day. It does not remove sign-in, emergency briefing or room-closing duties. A person who turns 16 next week is still under 16 on today's register. The guest office's youth host requirement therefore remains relevant whenever the cohort includes a younger student.

A visiting artist must not arrange private follow-up coaching with a minor through the minor's personal messaging account. Requests go to the office and the guardian receives the proposal. The artist can discuss a general class exercise during a supervised session, but should not exchange a private booking link or ask a student to hide a message. A guardian's presence on site does not automatically authorize an unrecorded private appointment.

Section: Guest Artist Office Handbook / Observation and access to rehearsal


## Observation and access to rehearsal
A visiting teacher may invite a colleague to observe from the marked bench. Observation has no teaching entitlement. The colleague cannot join a youth exercise, photograph participants or take attendance merely because the guest invited them. The host records the visitor's arrival and explains the exits. A late observer waits until the next natural break rather than crossing the dance floor during a sequence.

Every guest workshop containing any participant under 16 must have a rostered studio host present throughout the teaching period. This condition also applies to one-to-one coaching. A remote host available by telephone does not count as present. If the host must leave the building, teaching pauses until another rostered host takes over; the guest cannot waive this requirement.

Section: Guest Artist Office Handbook / Booking a visiting teacher


## Booking a visiting teacher
The guest office manages visiting artists who teach a short residency without joining the regular teaching rota. A guest session is attached to a named host teacher and a named room. The host remains responsible for the register, emergency information and closing the room; artistic leadership does not transfer these duties. An invitation email is an expression of interest until the guest office issues a numbered booking confirmation. Students must not infer a confirmed visit from a social post or a poster left over from a previous residency.

The guest office requires a visiting artist booking request at least 18 calendar days before the first workshop. A request records the teaching theme, room, age band, planned equipment and whether an observer will attend. Count the first teaching day as day zero. A request received on a weekend still receives its actual received date, but no appointment is held open while missing details are collected. The office offers a written alternative date when the requested lead time cannot be met.

Section: Guest Artist Office Handbook / Changing a confirmed workshop


## Changing a confirmed workshop
A confirmed guest workshop may be moved once without an administration fee if the host gives seven full days of notice. The change must retain the same visiting teacher and cohort. Replacing the guest, changing an adult class into a youth class, or adding a second day is a new booking request. A room change requested by building staff does not consume the host's one permitted move. The host sends the new room confirmation directly to enrolled participants and keeps the old message in the office record.

When a visiting artist cancels, the office offers either a replacement workshop or a full workshop-fee refund within ten business days. The office records each participant's choice. A regular class credit is not substituted without the participant's express choice. The ordinary timetable continues unless the host sends a separate message explaining an alteration; a cancelled guest event does not cancel an entire term of tuition.

## Scheduling details that do not change the booking
A studio rehearsal led by a regular teacher remains a regular rehearsal even if a guest sits at the side to watch. The office should not create a second workshop charge solely because a visiting artist is in the building. Conversely, an advertised guest workshop is not quietly converted to an ordinary class when the guest is delayed. The host explains the change and the office offers the recorded choices. Printed room plans show the expected sequence of activities, but the teacher can shorten a warm-up when safety requires it without changing the named booking identity.

Section: Guest Artist Office Handbook / Files, expenses and travel


## Files, expenses and travel
A guest supplies their public teaching biography as plain text. The office checks spelling before copying it to a studio event listing. Passport scans and bank details are collected through the private administration channel and never placed in the workshop plan. The booking number is sufficient in an attendance register; students do not need the guest's home address or travel route.

Travel arrangements belong to the signed visit agreement. The office handbook does not promise a hotel, luggage storage or reimbursement for a missed train. Where a train delay affects the class, the host first gives participants a revised start time, then records the actual teaching minutes. The host must not invent a shorter lesson and mark it delivered at full length.

## Cross-campus closing procedure

A host handover should tell the next adult what they need to do without filling a page with private details about the class. Start with the room and the time, then give the names of the adults who hold the key and the register. Note whether the guest has seen the exit route and knows where to find the first aid lead. Keep the music plan near the room notes so that a late change of device does not hold up the group. If the class shares a wall with a quiet activity, check the sound level from the hall before the students arrive. Tell the guest where to place a bag so that the door can open fully. A host who leaves for a short break must first tell the next host which students are present and whether anyone is due to arrive late. The next host should read back the room and group details to avoid a mistaken handover to a nearby class. Do not copy private phone numbers onto the public door sign. If a message needs to reach a guardian, use the office route and record the time it was sent. An artist may bring a paper plan for the lesson, but the host still keeps the studio register. A student's own note can explain a preferred cue, yet it does not replace the current support plan held by the office. When two rooms share a foyer, the host directs each group to the correct door rather than asking students to sort it out themselves. At the end of a session, allow time to check the room, collect lost items and tell the next teacher about any fault in the sound system. A worn cable is marked and set aside so that the next class does not discover the same fault by chance. The host must not unplug another room's working equipment to solve a local issue without speaking to that room's lead. If the artist needs a few more minutes to pack, move the conversation away from the class exit and keep the route clear. Students may ask for feedback at the desk, but the host should avoid a crowd forming around a guest who is trying to depart. A shared notebook can record the teaching theme and room layout while private student facts stay in the proper record. After the guest has left, check the floor for tape and return borrowed chairs to their marked places. The next host checks that the register folder is present before opening the room. Where the residency uses both the north and south buildings, the office compares the end of each room list with the next room's start list. It should not erase the earlier entry or imply the previous host saw information that arrived later. The office keeps the two room sheets together for the end of day check. Section: Percussion Loan Store Procedure / Cross-campus closing procedure


## Cross-campus closing procedure

A transfer between campuses is a move of a loan asset and should leave a clear trail even when the student who will borrow it has not yet arrived. The sending clerk checks the case number against the stock list and opens the case on a clear desk. Check that each beater is present and that the strap lies inside the case rather than across the hinge. Write down any mark already seen on the shell so that the next clerk does not mistake it for new damage. Close the lid and test the latch without putting weight on the drum. If the case has a loose hinge, use another inspected case and record both case numbers. The asset tag stays with the instrument and is not peeled off to make the case look tidy. A driver taking several kits reads the labels aloud with the sending clerk before loading. Put the heavier cases on the floor of the vehicle and keep them clear of loose chairs or bags. Do not stack a box of office files on top of a drum case merely because the lid looks flat. The receiving site should know which vehicle is coming and which adult will bring the equipment to the desk. An estimated arrival time is useful for planning but is not a proof that the instrument has been received. If the driver is delayed, tell the receiving clerk rather than leaving the cases outside a locked door. A student waiting for the drum can use a studio practice pad while staff arrange the actual handover. The student does not need to wait by the loading bay or contact the driver directly. When the kits reach the other campus, the receiving clerk checks each asset label before opening a case. Compare the contents with the sending note and inspect the strap and beaters again. A new rattle or a missing item is recorded at once so that the next lesson does not begin with an unexplained fault. Keep the transfer paperwork with the desk record rather than placing it loose inside a student's bag. The receiving clerk may ask the sending clerk to clarify a mark, but the student is not asked to settle a disagreement between sites. If the case is cold from the trip, let it reach room temperature before opening it for practice. A loan can be reserved before transfer, yet a reservation does not mean that the student has collected the item. Staff should distinguish the transport time from the period in the student's care. The driver returning an empty vehicle is not evidence that every kit was accepted at the other desk. Before closing the transfer task, compare the number of cases loaded with the number accepted. Any difference remains open until someone locates the asset and records the handover. A clerk who leaves at the end of a shift tells the next clerk which kits still need checking. The next clerk uses the same record rather than starting a new loan in order to clear a queue. The final step is the specific receiving signature rule stated at the end of this paragraph. For an instrument sent between campuses, the receiving clerk must sign the amber transfer card before the loan clock starts.

Section: Percussion Loan Store Procedure / Cross-campus closing procedure


## Cross-campus closing procedure

A transfer between campuses is a move of a loan asset and should leave a clear trail even when the student who will borrow it has not yet arrived. The sending clerk checks the case number against the stock list and opens the case on a clear desk. Check that each beater is present and that the strap lies inside the case rather than across the hinge. Write down any mark already seen on the shell so that the next clerk does not mistake it for new damage. Close the lid and test the latch without putting weight on the drum. If the case has a loose hinge, use another inspected case and record both case numbers. The asset tag stays with the instrument and is not peeled off to make the case look tidy. A driver taking several kits reads the labels aloud with the sending clerk before loading. Put the heavier cases on the floor of the vehicle and keep them clear of loose chairs or bags. Do not stack a box of office files on top of a drum case merely because the lid looks flat. The receiving site should know which vehicle is coming and which adult will bring the equipment to the desk. An estimated arrival time is useful for planning but is not a proof that the instrument has been received. If the driver is delayed, tell the receiving clerk rather than leaving the cases outside a locked door. A student waiting for the drum can use a studio practice pad while staff arrange the actual handover. The student does not need to wait by the loading bay or contact the driver directly. When the kits reach the other campus, the receiving clerk checks each asset label before opening a case. Compare the contents with the sending note and inspect the strap and beaters again. A new rattle or a missing item is recorded at once so that the next lesson does not begin with an unexplained fault. Keep the transfer paperwork with the desk record rather than placing it loose inside a student's bag. The receiving clerk may ask the sending clerk to clarify a mark, but the student is not asked to settle a disagreement between sites. If the case is cold from the trip, let it reach room temperature before opening it for practice. A loan can be reserved before transfer, yet a reservation does not mean that the student has collected the item. Staff should distinguish the transport time from the period in the student's care. The driver returning an empty vehicle is not evidence that every kit was accepted at the other desk. Before closing the transfer task, compare the number of cases loaded with the number accepted. Any difference remains open until someone locates the asset and records the handover. A clerk who leaves at the end of a shift tells the next clerk which kits still need checking. The next clerk uses the same record rather than starting a new loan in order to clear a queue. The final step is the specific receiving signature rule stated at the end of this paragraph. For an instrument sent between campuses, the receiving clerk must sign the amber transfer card before the loan clock starts.

## Caring for borrowed equipment
Borrowed percussion must be carried inside its closed case whenever it is outdoors, including in dry weather. The purpose is to protect tension fittings and prevent straps catching on doors. A case should not be left in a hot car or against a heater. If the drum gets wet, stop using it and contact the store before attempting to tighten the skin. Household oil, glue and adhesive tape are not approved repairs.

Hands should be clean and dry before practice. Keep drinks off the same table and allow the instrument to reach room temperature before opening a cold case. Use the supplied soft cloth for the shell only; a damp cloth suitable for a plastic practice pad may damage another surface. Store staff demonstrate the correct handling at collection and can repeat the explanation without extending the loan automatically.

Section: Loan Instrument Repair and Recall Checklist / Hygiene and consumables


## Hygiene and consumables
Practice-pad surfaces are cleaned with the supplied dry microfiber cloth after each use; students must not spray them with disinfectant. Bench staff use a separate manufacturer-approved process between borrowers. A sticky surface is reported rather than scrubbed with an abrasive sponge. Consumable tape used by a teacher to mark a rhythm pattern belongs on the practice mat, not on the borrowed instrument or its case label.

The repair record tracks replaced components and the person who performed the inspection. A drum can look unchanged after an internal fitting has been secured. Staff therefore check the inspection tag rather than inferring safety from appearance. A student is welcome to ask what was done, but cannot sign a workshop release on behalf of the repair technician.

Section: Percussion Loan Store Procedure / What the loan store provides


## What the loan store provides
The studio lends small hand drums, frame drums and practice pads for enrolled rhythm classes. Loan instruments are teaching equipment, not personal gifts. A label on the case identifies the asset number, kit contents and inspection date. A student borrows the entire listed kit so that the return can be checked against a clear inventory. A strap found loose in a room is not added to a kit without recording it.

A standard percussion instrument loan lasts 21 calendar days from the signed collection date. The collection day is day zero and the due date is written on the receipt. A student may return earlier without a fee. Returning the case to a teaching room is not a completed return; the store desk must inspect and acknowledge it. The receipt remains the reference if the timetable changes during the loan.

An enrolled student must reserve a loan instrument at least three business days before collection. A reservation names the intended class and required instrument size. The store may offer a practice pad when the requested drum is unavailable, but the student can decline that substitute. A teacher keeping equipment for a studio-led rehearsal uses the departmental checkout list instead of a student loan.

Section: Loan Instrument Repair and Recall Checklist / Opening a repair record


## Opening a repair record
A repair report identifies the asset number and describes what happened in ordinary language. Students need not name a component correctly. Staff distinguish an observed defect from a guess about its cause, then mark whether the instrument can remain in use. Photographs can help locate a mark, but a photograph alone does not establish that a student caused it. The repair bench is not a place for public arguments about responsibility.

A borrower must report a split drumhead or loose metal fitting within 24 hours of discovering it. Stop playing and keep the instrument in its case while waiting for instructions. A report can be lodged even when the desk is closed; record when the issue was noticed and when the message was sent. Do not attempt a test strike to make a crack easier to hear.

Section: Percussion Loan Store Procedure / Cross-campus closing procedure


## Cross-campus closing procedure

A transfer between campuses is a move of a loan asset and should leave a clear trail even when the student who will borrow it has not yet arrived. The sending clerk checks the case number against the stock list and opens the case on a clear desk. Check that each beater is present and that the strap lies inside the case rather than across the hinge. Write down any mark already seen on the shell so that the next clerk does not mistake it for new damage. Close the lid and test the latch without putting weight on the drum. If the case has a loose hinge, use another inspected case and record both case numbers. The asset tag stays with the instrument and is not peeled off to make the case look tidy. A driver taking several kits reads the labels aloud with the sending clerk before loading. Put the heavier cases on the floor of the vehicle and keep them clear of loose chairs or bags. Do not stack a box of office files on top of a drum case merely because the lid looks flat. The receiving site should know which vehicle is coming and which adult will bring the equipment to the desk. An estimated arrival time is useful for planning but is not a proof that the instrument has been received. If the driver is delayed, tell the receiving clerk rather than leaving the cases outside a locked door. A student waiting for the drum can use a studio practice pad while staff arrange the actual handover. The student does not need to wait by the loading bay or contact the driver directly. When the kits reach the other campus, the receiving clerk checks each asset label before opening a case. Compare the contents with the sending note and inspect the strap and beaters again. A new rattle or a missing item is recorded at once so that the next lesson does not begin with an unexplained fault. Keep the transfer paperwork with the desk record rather than placing it loose inside a student's bag. The receiving clerk may ask the sending clerk to clarify a mark, but the student is not asked to settle a disagreement between sites. If the case is cold from the trip, let it reach room temperature before opening it for practice. A loan can be reserved before transfer, yet a reservation does not mean that the student has collected the item. Staff should distinguish the transport time from the period in the student's care. The driver returning an empty vehicle is not evidence that every kit was accepted at the other desk. Before closing the transfer task, compare the number of cases loaded with the number accepted. Any difference remains open until someone locates the asset and records the handover. A clerk who leaves at the end of a shift tells the next clerk which kits still need checking. The next clerk uses the same record rather than starting a new loan in order to clear a queue. The final step is the specific receiving signature rule stated at the end of this paragraph. For an instrument sent between campuses, the receiving clerk must sign the amber transfer card before the loan clock starts.

Section: Percussion Loan Store Procedure / Cross-campus closing procedure


## Cross-campus closing procedure

A transfer between campuses is a move of a loan asset and should leave a clear trail even when the student who will borrow it has not yet arrived. The sending clerk checks the case number against the stock list and opens the case on a clear desk. Check that each beater is present and that the strap lies inside the case rather than across the hinge. Write down any mark already seen on the shell so that the next clerk does not mistake it for new damage. Close the lid and test the latch without putting weight on the drum. If the case has a loose hinge, use another inspected case and record both case numbers. The asset tag stays with the instrument and is not peeled off to make the case look tidy. A driver taking several kits reads the labels aloud with the sending clerk before loading. Put the heavier cases on the floor of the vehicle and keep them clear of loose chairs or bags. Do not stack a box of office files on top of a drum case merely because the lid looks flat. The receiving site should know which vehicle is coming and which adult will bring the equipment to the desk. An estimated arrival time is useful for planning but is not a proof that the instrument has been received. If the driver is delayed, tell the receiving clerk rather than leaving the cases outside a locked door. A student waiting for the drum can use a studio practice pad while staff arrange the actual handover. The student does not need to wait by the loading bay or contact the driver directly. When the kits reach the other campus, the receiving clerk checks each asset label before opening a case. Compare the contents with the sending note and inspect the strap and beaters again. A new rattle or a missing item is recorded at once so that the next lesson does not begin with an unexplained fault. Keep the transfer paperwork with the desk record rather than placing it loose inside a student's bag. The receiving clerk may ask the sending clerk to clarify a mark, but the student is not asked to settle a disagreement between sites. If the case is cold from the trip, let it reach room temperature before opening it for practice. A loan can be reserved before transfer, yet a reservation does not mean that the student has collected the item. Staff should distinguish the transport time from the period in the student's care. The driver returning an empty vehicle is not evidence that every kit was accepted at the other desk. Before closing the transfer task, compare the number of cases loaded with the number accepted. Any difference remains open until someone locates the asset and records the handover. A clerk who leaves at the end of a shift tells the next clerk which kits still need checking. The next clerk uses the same record rather than starting a new loan in order to clear a queue. The final step is the specific receiving signature rule stated at the end of this paragraph. For an instrument sent between campuses, the receiving clerk must sign the amber transfer card before the loan clock starts.

Section: Percussion Loan Store Procedure / What the loan store provides


## What the loan store provides
The studio lends small hand drums, frame drums and practice pads for enrolled rhythm classes. Loan instruments are teaching equipment, not personal gifts. A label on the case identifies the asset number, kit contents and inspection date. A student borrows the entire listed kit so that the return can be checked against a clear inventory. A strap found loose in a room is not added to a kit without recording it.

A standard percussion instrument loan lasts 21 calendar days from the signed collection date. The collection day is day zero and the due date is written on the receipt. A student may return earlier without a fee. Returning the case to a teaching room is not a completed return; the store desk must inspect and acknowledge it. The receipt remains the reference if the timetable changes during the loan.

An enrolled student must reserve a loan instrument at least three business days before collection. A reservation names the intended class and required instrument size. The store may offer a practice pad when the requested drum is unavailable, but the student can decline that substitute. A teacher keeping equipment for a studio-led rehearsal uses the departmental checkout list instead of a student loan.

## Hearing protection and the emergency signal
A student may wear their own ear defenders during ordinary class exercises after the teacher confirms a visible stop signal. The teacher rehearses the signal with the student before a sequence begins. The room-operation notes set a narrow condition during an evacuation drill; the ordinary class permission must be considered together with that condition. Headphones playing private music are not automatically covered by permission for passive ear defenders.

Teachers should give a spoken and visible cue for a planned loud activity. A student can choose an alternative position agreed in the plan. If the visibility arrangement fails, pause the activity and agree a workable signal rather than removing the student's support without explanation.

Section: Guest Artist Office Handbook / Booking a visiting teacher


## Booking a visiting teacher
The guest office manages visiting artists who teach a short residency without joining the regular teaching rota. A guest session is attached to a named host teacher and a named room. The host remains responsible for the register, emergency information and closing the room; artistic leadership does not transfer these duties. An invitation email is an expression of interest until the guest office issues a numbered booking confirmation. Students must not infer a confirmed visit from a social post or a poster left over from a previous residency.

The guest office requires a visiting artist booking request at least 18 calendar days before the first workshop. A request records the teaching theme, room, age band, planned equipment and whether an observer will attend. Count the first teaching day as day zero. A request received on a weekend still receives its actual received date, but no appointment is held open while missing details are collected. The office offers a written alternative date when the requested lead time cannot be met.

Section: Guest Artist Office Handbook / Changing a confirmed workshop


## Changing a confirmed workshop
A confirmed guest workshop may be moved once without an administration fee if the host gives seven full days of notice. The change must retain the same visiting teacher and cohort. Replacing the guest, changing an adult class into a youth class, or adding a second day is a new booking request. A room change requested by building staff does not consume the host's one permitted move. The host sends the new room confirmation directly to enrolled participants and keeps the old message in the office record.

When a visiting artist cancels, the office offers either a replacement workshop or a full workshop-fee refund within ten business days. The office records each participant's choice. A regular class credit is not substituted without the participant's express choice. The ordinary timetable continues unless the host sends a separate message explaining an alteration; a cancelled guest event does not cancel an entire term of tuition.

Section: Visiting Artist Welcome and Safeguarding Notes / Before the first visit


## Before the first visit
The welcome coordinator meets visiting artists at the front desk, explains the teaching rooms and identifies the staff host. The guest should arrive with the music already available on a device that can work offline. The desk can lend a cable, but it cannot guarantee a particular streaming service, account login or telephone signal. A teaching plan should contain an alternative quiet activity for a short audio failure.

Visiting artists must check in 25 minutes before their first scheduled teaching session. Return visits during the same confirmed residency use the normal staff sign-in process. The desk records the artist's preferred public name separately from any legal name needed for payment. Student-facing signs use the agreed public name only.

Section: Visiting Artist Welcome and Safeguarding Notes / Underage participants and private coaching


## Underage participants and private coaching
For an adult-only guest workshop, the artist may teach without a host in the room after the duty lead signs the adult-session exception. The exception is specific to the dated session and cannot be copied to a youth workshop later that day. It does not remove sign-in, emergency briefing or room-closing duties. A person who turns 16 next week is still under 16 on today's register. The guest office's youth host requirement therefore remains relevant whenever the cohort includes a younger student.

A visiting artist must not arrange private follow-up coaching with a minor through the minor's personal messaging account. Requests go to the office and the guardian receives the proposal. The artist can discuss a general class exercise during a supervised session, but should not exchange a private booking link or ask a student to hide a message. A guardian's presence on site does not automatically authorize an unrecorded private appointment.

## Shared teaching and shortened sessions
If the named guest is replaced by another artist, a fresh booking confirmation is required even when the workshop title stays the same. The replacement supplies a new biography and receives their own host briefing. Students can then decide whether the revised event suits them under the office's cancellation offer. A guest's assistant leading a five-minute demonstration while the guest remains present is recorded as support, not as a hidden replacement.

Section: Guest Artist Office Handbook / Observation and access to rehearsal


## Observation and access to rehearsal
A visiting teacher may invite a colleague to observe from the marked bench. Observation has no teaching entitlement. The colleague cannot join a youth exercise, photograph participants or take attendance merely because the guest invited them. The host records the visitor's arrival and explains the exits. A late observer waits until the next natural break rather than crossing the dance floor during a sequence.

Every guest workshop containing any participant under 16 must have a rostered studio host present throughout the teaching period. This condition also applies to one-to-one coaching. A remote host available by telephone does not count as present. If the host must leave the building, teaching pauses until another rostered host takes over; the guest cannot waive this requirement.
